title: Operator playlet bundler and catalog for composable admin tasks
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem:
Support engineers and oncall frequently need small, composable admin operations (check status, rotate keys, scale a service, collect diagnostics). Today these are ad-hoc shell scripts or long runbooks that require manual steps and context switching. We lack a standardized, discoverable artifact format for small, safe, idempotent admin actions that can be composed into larger flows or executed standalone from the CLI/console.

Proposal:
Create an 'operator playlet' bundler and catalog: a lightweight package format (manifest + optional script + typed inputs) for idempotent, parameterized admin actions. Playlets will be linted for safety (principle of least privilege, idempotency hints), simulated in a dry-run sandbox, and published into a searchable catalog in the Console. The bundler will produce immutable versioned artifacts (playlet: name/version/hash) and a manifest that the admin runtime (opsctl/console-runner) can execute with a --dry-run flag.

Scope and deliverables:
- Define playlet manifest schema (metadata, inputs, required roles, expected side effects, idempotency level).
- Implement bundler CLI that packages playlets, signs metadata, and publishes to internal S3-backed catalog.
- Console catalog UI extension (search + tags + preview + dry-run simulation link). Minimal stubbed integration: catalog serves JSON manifest and executable artifacts.
- Runtime hooks in opsctl to fetch a playlet by name@version and execute with telemetry and safety envelope (prompt for escalation if input exceeds thresholds).
- Linter rules for safety checks and a CI job that rejects playlets missing metadata or with unsafe commands.
- Migration path: convert 6 most-used ad-hoc scripts into playlets as examples and templates for the team.

Non-goals:
- Full visual playflow composer (out of scope for this ticket; follow-ups will cover visual editor).

Acceptance criteria:
- Manifest schema doc committed to docs/confluence with examples.
- bundler CLI (playlet-pack) able to package a playlet and publish to internal catalog endpoint. End-to-end demo: package + publish + install + dry-run on staging cluster.
- opsctl can execute a playlet by explicit name@version and honor --dry-run and --force flags.
- Linter CI gate that fails on an intentionally unsafe example (e.g., missing required role or executing destructive command without confirmation metadata).
- 6 converted example playlets checked in under ops/playlets/ with PRs and linked runbook notes.
- Telemetry sent to admin-playlets dashboard: executions, dry-run vs live count, failures, and time-to-complete.

Telemetry & SLOs:
- Track per-playlet success rate and average execution time. Alert if success rate drops below 95% for a published playlet used >10 times/day.
- Add cost tag to manifest so we can filter high-cost playlets when building runbook rollouts.

Security & compliance:
- Playlet manifests must include required IAM roles and KMS usage when accessing secrets. Bundler will fail if secret references are not tagged with purpose.
- security_review_required: true. We'll coordinate with Security to define allowed primitive commands for playlets.

Rollout plan:
1) RFC + manifest schema (this ticket).
2) Implement bundler + linter + CI gate (alpha users only).
3) Convert 6 canonical scripts into playlets; validate telemetry.
4) Console catalog MVP and opsctl runtime hook.
5) Gradual rollout to production teams with opt-in and training docs.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Playlets could be used to automate dangerous actions at scale. Mitigation: default playlets run with least-privileged role; require explicit escalation and human confirmation for destructive scopes; safety linter + runtime thresholds.
- Risk: Fragmentation if teams define diverging manifest conventions. Mitigation: keep schema minimal, ship reference templates, and require central catalog publishing for discoverability.

Owner notes:
- We'll reuse parts of the admin packaging code from ENG-314159's runbook scheduler for packaging conventions but maintain a separate lightweight manifest (no heavy DSL).
- Work with UX to provide a compact preview display in Console that shows inputs, outputs, and recent runs.

Next steps (technical):
- Draft manifest schema (examples: check-db-health v0.1, rotate-service-key v0.2).
- Spike: implement dry-run sandbox for shell playlets in a K8s namespace with resource limits.
- Create CI linter rules and a sample failing test.
- Schedule 1:1 with Security to review allowed primitives and signing expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest schema RFC merged to docs repository
playlet-pack CLI can create and publish a package to the internal catalog endpoint
opsctl can fetch and execute a playlet by name@version with --dry-run and --force flags
CI linter rejects an unsafe playlet example
Six example playlets converted, with PRs and runbook links
Dashboard shows executions and failure rate for published playlets
